clue.text: Entertainer loses head, confronted by wealthy bird

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a host entertains guests
wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: A performer who has lost their top billing finds themselves up against a rich rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' takes the H off HOST, leaving OST; 'confronted by' just sets RICH beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a large flightless African species of the avian class.

clue.text: Public controversy about introduction of hen run

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go round the next one

parts.note: overt means public, done openly
a row is a controversy or quarrel

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A public dispute over bringing in a chicken run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the phrase for 'Public controversy' round the letter from 'introduction of hen'. In cricket a fielder's wild return can concede extra runs.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an overthrow is a run scored when the fielder's return goes astray.

clue.text: Student absorbs beginning of course, in the end

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed: 'Student absorbs beginning of course, in the end (7)'. TEE (beginning of a golf course) round RAIN fits, but no clue word gives RAIN; the scan agrees and no search found the parse.

clue.text: Priest in Bury initially engaged to mediate

indicators.note: in means the priest is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon, a priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman in a Lancashire town is first to get involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town, but it is the verb. Ven (Venerable) is an archdeacon's title.
explanation.definitionFit: To intervene is to step in between parties, to mediate.

clue.text: Way in which a fair number give vent to primitive emotions

parts.note: how means the way in which
L is the Roman numeral fifty, a fair number

explanation.surface: A large crowd find a way to let out their basest feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: L is 50 in Roman numerals, which the clue calls 'a fair number'.
explanation.definitionFit: To howl is to cry out in a long wail, a raw outburst of feeling.

clue.text: Publication carrying letters from Bali in this

definitions.text: Publication carrying letters from Bali in this

indicators.note: carrying means the magazine holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a magazine, MAG for short, is a publication

indicators.note: the letters from the word Bali are taken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A magazine reporting on a sack full of post sent from an Indonesian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters from' signals ILBA, which 'carrying' places between the second and third letters of the publication. Read whole, the clue also pictures a sack of airmail.
explanation.definitionFit: A postal sack holds correspondence, including airmail from distant islands.

clue.text: Commercial vessel lit up in lake

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the lake

parts.note: a mere is a lake
a can is a vessel

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A trading ship is lit up on the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LIT into TIL; CAN and TIL then go 'in' MERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile means relating to trade and merchants.

clue.text: Discharge choir for inaccurate rendering

indicators.note: an inaccurate rendering of the word choir puts its letters in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A choir is sacked for singing out of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' looks like a dismissal, but it is the noun: the watery fluid from a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichor is a thin, watery fluid oozing from a wound or sore.

clue.text: Rock for the more enterprising, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word is spoken and its sound gives the spelling

parts.note: bolder means more enterprising or daring

explanation.surface: Rock climbing suits the more adventurous, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: BOLDER spoken sounds like the answer, a large rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A boulder is a large stone, a lump of rock worn smooth.

clue.text: Fresh intelligence about soldiers

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or intelligence
RE is the Royal Engineers, soldiers

explanation.surface: New information on the troops comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) is the usual crossword soldiery; GEN is British slang for the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means fresh, new or unripe, as in green wood.

clue.text: Acclaim cut rejected by leftist extremists

indicators.note: rejected here means turned back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it

indicators.note: the extremists of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Praise for a spending cut gets turned down by radical left-wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns AXE into EXA; 'extremists' of 'leftist' are its first and last letters, L and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim someone is to praise them highly, to glorify them.

clue.text: Which people are admitted to utilise this repository?

indicators.note: being admitted to a place means going inside it

parts.note: who means which people
taken as written
to utilise is to use

explanation.surface: A question about who is allowed in to make use of a storage building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Which people' looks like a question opener but supplies a word; 'admitted to' is the container signal and 'this' only points at the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A warehouse is a large building where goods are stored.

clue.text: Fish circling the way back from Arctic region

indicators.note: circling means the first piece goes all round the second

parts.note: the tuna is a fish

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A fish swims round on its way home from the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the road abbreviation round to DR before 'circling' places it inside the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the treeless, frozen plain found in the far north.

clue.text: Old scold said to trouble Jacob's son

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken and the sound gives the spelling

parts.note: to harry is to trouble, and Dan was one of the twelve sons of Jacob in Genesis

explanation.surface: A nagging old woman is reported to pester one of the patriarch's sons.
explanation.walkthrough: HARRY DAN spoken aloud sounds like the answer, a term for a bad-tempered old woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, nagging old woman, a crone given to scolding.

clue.text: An early believer in world revolution

definitions.text: An early believer in world revolution

parts.words: An early believer in world revolution
parts.note: not a political radical but a Renaissance astronomer who held that the earth revolves round the sun

explanation.walkthrough: 'world revolution' sounds like global political upheaval, but it is the earth's orbit round the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish astronomer proposed that the planets, earth among them, orbit the sun.

clue.text: Rough-sounding mate for this flighty female

definitions.text: Rough-sounding mate for this flighty female

parts.words: Rough-sounding mate for this flighty female
parts.note: the male of this female bird is the ruff, which sounds like rough; flighty because she can fly

explanation.walkthrough: The ruff is a wading bird; its female has her own name. 'Rough-sounding' points at the male's name, and 'flighty' is a joke on a bird that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve is the female of the ruff, a sandpiper of marshes and meadows.

clue.text: Striking garments evident in the suburbs

parts.note: workers who are striking are out
skirts are garments

explanation.surface: Eye-catching clothes are on show in the residential areas around town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like 'eye-catching', but it means on strike, OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The outskirts are the outer areas of a town, where its suburbs lie.

clue.text: Activate engine to make punt get underway

parts.note: a punt is a kick, in rugby or American football
to start is to get underway

explanation.surface: Fire up an outboard motor to get a river boat moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' looks like the boat but is a kick of the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Kick-starting a motorcycle means turning its engine over with a foot pedal.

clue.text: Way to restrain monster going berserk nearest the rear

indicators.note: to restrain means to hold in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: going berserk means the word monster runs wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A way to hold back a monster that has run amok at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going berserk' makes TERNMOS, which 'to restrain' holds inside the street abbreviation. The page prints the indicator as 'beserk'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternmost means furthest aft, closest to the back of a ship.

clue.text: This grain, and nothing else, for breakfast?

definitions.text: This grain, and nothing else, for breakfast?

parts.words: This grain, and nothing else, for breakfast?
parts.note: read as an entire repast made only of grain, the clue describes flour with nothing removed

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words the answer suggests a complete repast; as one word it is flour or bread using the entire grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholemeal flour is milled from the entire grain, bran and germ included.

clue.text: No place like Pittsburgh engenders such dullness

parts.note: O, a zero, means no
Pittsburgh is a city in Pennsylvania, abbreviated PA, so a PA city

explanation.surface: Nowhere is as drab as Pittsburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania, the US state where Pittsburgh is.
explanation.definitionFit: Opacity means lack of clarity, obscurity or dullness of understanding.

clue.text: Accountant's note read in class

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant, and the 's adds an S
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An auditor's memo is read out to a classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: CA (chartered accountant) with its 's gives CAS; TE (also spelt ti) is the seventh sol-fa note.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social rank, a class in a rigid hierarchy.

clue.text: Cut hair of individual, say, when drunk?

indicators.note: slurred speech turns an s sound into sh

parts.note: single means individual

explanation.surface: A tipsy person asks for a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk slurs SINGLE into SHINGLE; the question mark flags the whimsy. To shingle hair is to cut it short and tapered.
explanation.definitionFit: To shingle is to crop the hair short at the back of the head.

clue.text: Inclination to accept king's scholarship

indicators.note: to accept means to take something in, so the king goes inside

parts.note: a leaning is an inclination
R, for rex, stands for a king

explanation.surface: A tendency to take up a royal grant for study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts R (rex, Latin for king) inside LEANING.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarship here means erudition, knowledge gained by study.

clue.text: Source of forgetfulness for many superior to you and me

indicators.note: superior to in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a lot means many
us means you and me

explanation.surface: Many people are said to have more power than ordinary folk like us.
explanation.walkthrough: In Homer's Odyssey the lotus fruit made those who ate it forget home.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the lotus fruit induced a dreamy oblivion in those who ate it.

clue.text: Illustrious philanthropist turns tail

indicators.note: turns tail means the final pair of letters is swapped round

parts.note: Alfred Nobel, founder of the Nobel Prizes, was a philanthropist

explanation.surface: A well-known benefactor runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns tail' swaps the last two letters of NOBEL, giving NOBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble means illustrious, of high rank or fine character.

clue.text: Fix a second information board .

parts.note: a sign is a board giving information

explanation.surface: Someone puts up a second noticeboard.
explanation.walkthrough: A, S for second, and SIGN for a board that informs, in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign is to fix or allot, as in fixing a date or a task.

clue.text: Door-keeper ejects hard drug addict

indicators.note: ejects means a letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: an usher keeps the door at a court or theatre
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A bouncer throws out an addict hooked on hard drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ejects' takes H (hard) out of USHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is someone who takes drugs habitually.

clue.text: They may delay the progress of advocate in formal wear

indicators.note: in means the second word is placed inside the first

parts.note: tails are a formal evening coat
to back a cause is to advocate it

explanation.surface: A barrister in tailcoat and wig holds up proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advocate' looks like a lawyer, but it is the verb meaning support; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailbacks are queues of traffic stretching back, slowing travel down.

clue.text: Belligerent behaviour of some 5 ac groups

clue.text: Lack of confidence displayed by Head after gibe

indicators.note: after means the headland comes after the gibe in the answer

parts.note: a shy is a throw, and figuratively a gibe or jeer
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A boss's timidity shows after a taunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a person but is NESS, a headland. SHY as a gibe is a dated sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Shyness is timidity, the want of self-assurance.

clue.text: It is not unbeatable as a place of shelter

definitions.meaning: one beats a hasty withdrawal, so it is something that can be beaten

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is to 'beat a retreat', so the word is literally beatable.
explanation.definitionFit: Armies beat a withdrawal, and the same word names a secluded refuge.
